{{Quote|Good girl, Boga.|[[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]]|<ref name="ROTS novel">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref>}}
'''Boga''' was a [[Gender/Legends|female]] [[Varactyl/Legends|varactyl]] native to [[Utapau/Legends|Utapau]]. Like all members of her species, she was a large reptilian quadruped with a beaked maw and feathers splaying from her scaled skin.

==Biography==

===Early Life===
[[File:Kenobiandboga.jpg|thumb|right|175px|Boga and Obi-wan plummet down the ravine.]]

A smart and loyal creature,<ref name=":0">''[[Star Wars: Head-to-Head]]''</ref> Boga was one of the fastest varactyl to be tamed by the [[Utai/Legends|Utai]] beast tamers. She was thirty-nine hands tall at her shoulder, fifteen meters in length, and possessed a magnificent crest of blue, purple and green feathers.

===Battle of Utapau===
During his search for [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] on Utapau, [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] chose Boga as his mount. Astride Boga, Obi-Wan reached the tenth level of [[Tion Medon/Legends|Tion Medon's]] [[Pau City/Legends|Pau City]] in record time. Boga proved a worthy match for General Grievous in his [[Tsmeu-6 personal wheel bike|wheel bike]], chasing the [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] general through the city and using her clawed feet to climb the sinkhole walls in pursuit. Along the way, she proved valuable to Obi-Wan, disabling Grievous's [[Sheathipede-class transport shuttle/Legends|shuttle]] and picking off several droids. With Boga's help, Obi-Wan confronted and destroyed the General.<ref name=":1">{{Film|III}}</ref>

Unfortunately for Boga, the [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] turned against her [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] rider on the [[Order 66/Legends|orders]] of [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]]. Boga and Obi-Wan were caught in an explosion caused by an [[All Terrain Tactical Enforcer/Legends|AT-TE]], sending both plummeting into the water at the bottom of the sinkhole.<ref name=":1" /> Obi-Wan had assumed that Boga died,<ref name="ROTS novel" /> but she actually survived the fall slinking off to recover from her wounds and rejoined her stable mates long after the battle was over.<ref name="Fact File 37">{{FactFile2014|37|UTA 1-6|Utapau}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==

===Conception===
During Pre-Production for [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']], [[George Lucas]] had originally chosen Boga to be [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker's]] mount.<ref name="Making Revenge">''[[The Making of Star Wars Revenge of the Sith]]''</ref> However, it was soon dropped by the rough draft.<ref name="Making Revenge" />
[[File:Boga_concept.jpg|thumb|250x250px|An early concept of Boga.]]
The creation of Boga proved to be one of the most daunting animation challenges of Episode III, as an active, agile digital creature had to be married to relatively static live action footage of Ewan McGregor atop a practical saddle. Originally, Visual Effects Supervisor John Knoll had hoped the Boga sequences would be pushed to later in the schedule, to the 2004 pick-up photography, allowing time to develop a system where digital animation would drive the practical rig ridden by McGregor. Lucas, however, insisted on shooting McGregor's lizard-riding action during the 2003 principal photography window. Animation Director Rob Coleman worked with the Animatics Department to refine Boga's run cycle, studying nature footage of various running lizards as inspiration to the shooting crew. When it came time to shoot the live action elements of the Utapau chase in September of '03, a blue-painted barrel-shaped hydraulic rig stood in for Boga. The gimbal rig controlled by the Special Effects Department under the supervision of Dave Young could rock and buck at a good speed, but it wasn't set to precisely mimic the swaying run cycle of the animatic Boga. This created the need for extensive repositioning and massaging of the live action element of Obi-Wan when it was composited atop the striding beast. In cases where Boga's movements were very extreme, Obi-Wan was entirely computer-generated as no live action element could ever properly match Boga's agility. Aside from getting a live action Obi-Wan to realistically serve as jockey to Boga, the creature's size and speed proved a challenge as well. With its long neck and tail fully unfurled, the creature's length spanned about fifty feet, yet it had to be fleet-footed enough to run with Grievous' wheel bike.<ref name="DB-Boga">{{DB|creature|boga|Boga}}</ref>

The sound of Boga was created from the sounds of a dog, a [[Skywalker Ranch]] coyote and a Tasmanian Devil (which was originally recorded for [[Willow (film)|''Willow'']]).<ref name="Drawing from the Present: Familiar Creatures in a Galaxy Far, Far Away">{{SW|url=news/drawing-from-the-present-familiar-creatures-in-a-galaxy-far-far-away|text=Drawing from the Present: Familiar Creatures in a Galaxy Far, Far Away|int=Back from the Drawing Board|nolive=1}}</ref>

"Boga" was the name of a soft drink found in [[Wikipedia:Tunisia|Tunisia]] that the crew became familiar with during the filming of ''A New Hope'', and it was after this that the varactyl Boga, as well as the beverage [[Boga noga/Legends|Boga noga]], was named (see also [[Tunisia]] for other Tunisian-inspired names).

===Differences in adaptations===
In the [[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]], Obi-Wan believed Boga had died, and took a moment to reflect on her believed sacrifice.<ref name="ROTS novel" /> However, later it was established that Boga survived.<ref name="Fact File 37" /> In the novelization Boga takes the brunt of the clone trooper's blast, protecting Kenobi,<ref name="ROTS novel" /> but in the comic it is the opposite, showing Kenobi blocking laser fire, attempting to protect Boga.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode III — Revenge of the Sith 3">[[Star Wars: Episode III — Revenge of the Sith 3|''Star Wars: Episode III — Revenge of the Sith'' 3]]</ref>

===Legacy===
Some fans believe that the reason Obi-Wan's yell to ward off the [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Sand People]] in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']] was changed in the DVD version was to make it seem that Obi-Wan was copying Boga's yelp.

In the ''[[Star Wars: Head-to-Head]]'' book, it is proven by experts that, in a case of Boga vs. the [[Acklay/Legends|Acklay]], Boga wins because she is smarter, more loyal, and able to outmaneuver the fast acklay.<ref name=":0" />
